title: About this project
name: Abandoned, But Not Forgotten
purpose: A child-friendly archive connecting Apollo 11, Viking 1 and Sojourner with original NASA evidence and the stories of equipment left behind.

tools.name: OpenAI Codex
tools.use: AI-assisted software development, explanatory text and implementation checks.

tools.name: OpenAI ImageGen
tools.use: AI-generated illustrated rooms, interface artwork and fictional guide characters.

tools.name: ChatGPT + Kling AI
tools.use: Owner-supplied AI-generated illustrated arrival films; not original NASA footage.

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.use: Owner-declared narrator production workflow. Six mission story/CRT recordings, three Last Signal messages and the Sojourner naming story are distinguished from historical spacecraft transmissions; per-file provenance is recorded separately.

audioTerms: The owner confirms paid-plan production for Suno and ElevenLabs. Their service terms apply to those recordings; they are separate from the project's code license.

archives.name: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA)
archives.use: Mission identities, hardware, landing regions and mission history, with direct Master Catalog records shown in every Where is it now? card. Later orbital images and follow-up research are credited separately.

archives.name: NASA Science, NASA History and JPL
archives.use: Mission accounts and original photographs. Each exhibit links its evidence and image credits.

archives.name: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS)
archives.use: Measured Viking pressure data and documented mission context. No synthetic measurements are presented.

archives.name: NASA 3D Resources
archives.use: Original Apollo and Viking models credited to NASA / Michael D. Carbajal. Viewing colors and lighting are adjusted; educational Sojourner and Pathfinder reconstructions are project-authored.

archives.name: NASA/JPL — On a Mission
archives.use: First Steps: Sojourner podcast excerpts and transcripts in the cassette, separately credited from synthetic narration.

archives.name: NASA Historical Sounds and Apollo Lunar Surface Journal
archives.use: Original short Eagle landing audio and timestamped transcript excerpts, kept distinct from modern narrator recordings.

software: Three.js (MIT), Draco (Apache-2.0), FFmpeg for media processing, esbuild for the viewer bundle and Playwright for browser checks. Kalam Bold headings, Patrick Hand body text and Share Tech Mono CRT text use the SIL Open Font License.
license: Apache-2.0 covers project-authored code. NASA evidence, original models, fonts, supplied media and generated recordings retain their own credits and applicable terms.
distinction: Illustrated scenes and smiling characters are creative guides, not historical photographs. Real NASA images, measurements and recordings are credited individually. This is an independent team project, not a NASA product or endorsement. Diskettes and CDs are imagined retrospective story archive controls, not a claim that those formats were used by the original missions.
humanContribution: The team chose the missions and NASA source pool, directed the visual style and interactions, supplied the films and narrator recordings, and reviewed and refined the experience. AI tools assisted production; they did not supply original scientific measurements.
